title: Why do traffic jams appear out of nowhere?
question: Why do traffic jams appear out of nowhere?
audience: Anyone who drives or rides in traffic, watching on X or Reddit, anywhere in the world. They have sat in a jam with no visible cause; they think jams need a crash, roadworks or a bottleneck.
promise: With enough cars close together, one small slowdown grows from driver to driver into a jam that slides backwards while the cars go forwards; leaving a big gap and holding a steady speed soaks the wave up instead of passing it on.

look.mood: Night on a test track: the kit's graphite stage as the dark ground, the road a lit band of asphalt, the cars lit 3D models with glowing tail lights. Red (the accent) is braking and the jam, nothing else; cyan is the car that soaks the wave up, and the driver who started it. The stage light sits on the jam and follows it.

music.note: A bed composed after the take, to the film's length; the cuts follow the voice.

facts.claim: In the experiment 22 cars drove on a single-lane circular road 230 m around, on flat ground with no bottleneck; they started almost evenly spaced at about 30 km/h, the drivers asked to cruise at about 30 km/h and to follow the car ahead safely. Published 4 March 2008. The gap between cars: 230 / 22 = 10.45 m front to front; with cars 4.5 m long (the model's assumption), about 6 m (5.95 m) bumper to bumper.
facts.source: Sugiyama, Fukui, Kikuchi, Hasebe, Nakayama, Nishinari, Tadaki and Yukawa, 'Traffic jams without bottlenecks: experimental evidence for the physical mechanism of the formation of a jam', New Journal of Physics 10 (2008) 033001 (read in full from the open-access copy, University of Osaka repository hdl.handle.net/11094/93262). The experiment was run at the track of Nakanihon Automotive College, Japan.

facts.claim: Small fluctuations grew until free flow broke down: the paper's snapshot 3 minutes after the start shows a jam, and several cars were forced to stop completely for a moment. The paper's point: a jam forms spontaneously once the density of cars passes a critical value; a bottleneck is only a trigger. The film's 'within minutes' and 'stopping dead' are these.
facts.source: Sugiyama et al. 2008 (f1), abstract, text and figure 3.

facts.claim: The jam cluster moved backwards at roughly 20 km/h while the cars kept going forwards (outside the jam at about 40 km/h); about 20 km/h is the common speed of jams measured on real highways (the paper compares it with aerial traces of highway traffic, Treiterer and Myers 1974).
facts.source: Sugiyama et al. 2008 (f1), text and figures 4 and 5.

facts.claim: The chain from one small slowdown to a stop is the film's model, not a measurement from the experiment: in sim.py one driver eases off from 30 to 25 km/h (-0.5 m/s2 for 3 s); as the slowdown passes back, the lowest speed of each driver it reaches is 24.6, 24.9, 24.8, 24.7, 24.5, 24.3, 24.0, 23.6, 23.1, 22.5, 21.8, 20.9, 19.9, 18.5, 16.5, 13.6, 8.7, 1.9, 0.0 km/h: the first few about the same, then each lower, until the 19th driver stops. Simplification said in words: 'the drivers behind react late and brake harder'.

The ring on screen is a computer model, labelled as one: 22 cars 4.5 m long on a 230 m ring, Intelligent Driver Model (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) with a 0.35 s reaction delay, parameters set so that 30 km/h at this spacing is steady. Its jam moves -18.5 km/h (backwards), close to the experiment's 20; cars outside reach 50.3 km/h (the experiment: about 40); about 11.0 cars are stopped at a time (the experiment's jam held about 5). The model's first car stops 20 s after the slowdown; the real drivers took a few minutes, so the film never shows the model's clock, and its sped-up passages are tagged.
facts.source: sim.py and sim.json (this film); Treiber, Hennecke, Helbing, Phys. Rev. E 62, 1805 (2000).

facts.claim: In a later ring experiment (260 m, 21 to 22 cars, run by the University of Arizona, USA), one car whose speed was controlled by a computer (a human still steered) dampened the stop-and-go waves; one of its controllers simply estimated the average speed and drove at it, letting the gap ahead open when the car in front sped up and close when it slowed. 'One car with a computer on the pedals' is that car. The driving advice (a big gap, a steady speed, don't copy the brakes ahead) is what that controller does; the film does not claim a human study.
facts.source: Stern et al., 'Dissipation of stop-and-go waves via control of autonomous vehicles: Field experiments', Transportation Research Part C 89 (2018) 205-221 (read in full, arXiv:1705.01693), sections 2.1 and 3.2.

facts.claim: In the film's model, one car (car 11) switched to that controller 140 s in (holding the ring's measured average, 12.5 km/h, and a long gap) smooths the ring: the spread of speeds over a minute falls from 18.76 km/h to 0.0 km/h. The car ahead of it stops and starts; it and the cars behind it roll at an even speed.
'Enough cars, close together' is the critical density of f2; '≈ 6 m' on screen is the ring's 5.95 m bumper-to-bumper gap (f1).
facts.source: Sugiyama et al. 2008; arithmetic in f1.

acts.title: Out of nowhere
acts.goal: The question, over a jam on an open road with no cause in sight.

acts.title: The surprise
acts.goal: Break the belief: no cause is needed, only enough cars close together.

acts.title: The ring
acts.goal: The 2008 experiment: 22 cars, a 230 m ring, 30 km/h, and still a jam.

acts.title: Why
acts.goal: One small slowdown grows from driver to driver until a car stops.

acts.title: The wave
acts.goal: The jam travels backwards at about 20 km/h while every car goes forwards, as on real highways.

acts.title: The fix
acts.goal: A big gap and a steady speed soak the wave up; one automated car did it for a whole ring.

acts.title: Recap
acts.goal: The three ideas in one frame, and the line to remember.

shots.voice: [curious] Why do traffic jams appear *out of nowhere?*
shots.teaches: Asks the one question, over the thing itself: a queue of brake lights on an open road.
shots.screen: Night. The 3D road (the ring of sim.py opened into a straight lane and repeated), seen low from behind a queue of crawling cars, every brake light lit and blooming. The question in metal type across the top third.
shots.motion: The camera creeps forward along the queue; the title types in by character and a sheen crosses 'out of nowhere?'.
shots.transition: The camera rises; the title lifts away.
shots.sound: The bed starts at full level on frame 0; a soft low hit under the title.
shots.check: Frame 0 finished; brake lights read red, not orange; title contrast.

frames.note: Frame 0 is finished: night, low behind a queue of cars on an open road, every brake light lit. The question is already landing across the top.

draw.text:
Why do traffic jams appear
out of nowhere?

frames.note: Midway: The camera creeps forward along the queue; the title types in by character and a sheen crosses 'out of nowhere?'.

draw.text:
Why do traffic jams appear
out of nowhere?

frames.note: The question has landed; the camera keeps creeping along the queue. Cut: the camera rises.

draw.text:
Why do traffic jams appear
out of nowhere?

draw.cut: the title lifts away as the camera rises

shots.voice: You crawl along, then the road clears.
shots.teaches: Names the experience: the jam ends and the road ahead is empty.
shots.screen: The camera flies low along the queue to its front, where cars pull away, lights off, onto open road.
shots.motion: A forward camera move along the lane, accelerating as the cars do.
shots.transition: The camera tilts down over the empty road.
shots.sound: A soft whoosh as the camera clears the front of the jam.
shots.check: The front of the jam visibly releases cars.

frames.note: Higher and behind: the queue crawls (red lights), and far ahead the road is clear.
Midway: A forward camera move along the lane, accelerating as the cars do.
Past the front of the jam: cars pull away, brake lights off, open road. Cut on 'clears'.

shots.voice: No crash, no roadworks, nothing.
shots.teaches: Rules out the usual causes.
shots.screen: Above the jam's front looking down the empty lane; two glass chips, 'no crash' and 'no roadworks', each struck through as it is said.
shots.motion: Chips pop in on their words; a strike line draws across each.
shots.transition: Pull back high to see the whole packed road.
shots.sound: Two small ticks between the words.
shots.check: Chips 30 px or more; nothing on the road ahead.

frames.note: Above the front of the jam, looking down the empty road: nothing is there.
Midway: Chips pop in on their words; a strike line draws across each.
The chips land and are struck through, one on each word; the road stays empty. Cut: pull back to the whole road.

shots.voice: [excited] Here's the surprise: enough cars, close together,
shots.teaches: The turn: density alone is enough.
shots.screen: High above the straight road, side on: one lane full of moving cars; the gap between two of them bracketed '≈ 6 m'.
shots.motion: The camera pulls up and turns side on; the bracket draws on 'close together'.
shots.transition: Brake lights begin to spread in the middle.
shots.sound: THE TURN: a soft impact on 'surprise'.
shots.check: The bracket matches the model's 5.95 m gap.

frames.note: High above the road, seen from the side: one lane, packed with cars all moving.
Midway: The camera pulls up and turns side on; the bracket draws on 'close together'.
On 'close together': the gap between two cars is bracketed, about six metres.

shots.voice: make the jam themselves.
shots.teaches: Nothing else is needed: the jam grows among the cars.
shots.screen: The same side view: a block of red brake lights forms among the moving cars and grows.
shots.motion: Brake lights spread backwards car by car (the model's own jam).
shots.transition: The road bends: it curls into a ring.
shots.sound: Nothing over the words; the bed alone.
shots.check: The cluster grows among cars, not at any obstacle.

frames.note: The same road: a cluster of brake lights starts in the middle of the packed cars.
Midway: Brake lights spread backwards car by car (the model's own jam).
The jam is there, made by nothing but the cars. Cut: the road starts to bend.

draw.cut: the road bends into a ring

shots.voice: [warmly] In two thousand eight, Japanese scientists tested it.
shots.teaches: Sets up the experiment that proved it.
shots.screen: The straight lane curls into a closed ring, seen from above at an angle: the test track. Source chip top left: 'Sugiyama et al., 2008 · New Journal of Physics'.
shots.motion: The road's curvature runs from 0 to a full circle while the camera rises; the cars ride it.
shots.transition: Hold on the closed ring while the labels arrive.
shots.sound: A long soft whoosh under the curl, between the words.
shots.check: No double road at the ends while curling.

frames.note: The road curls: the straight lane bends, the ends sweep round toward each other.
Half way: a horseshoe; the source chip lands top left.
Closed: the test track, a single lane ring, seen from above at an angle.

shots.voice: Twenty-two cars, on a ring two hundred and thirty metres around.
shots.teaches: The setup in numbers.
shots.screen: The ring fills the frame, 22 cars evenly spaced; chip '22 cars' at the centre, then a cyan arc measures the lane and a chip '230 m around'.
shots.motion: A slow orbit round the ring as the cars cruise; each chip lands on its number and the cyan arc draws round the lane.
shots.transition: Push in to one side.
shots.sound: A tick on each chip.
shots.check: 22 cars exactly; spacing even.

frames.note: The ring fills the frame, 22 cars evenly spaced and all moving.
On 'twenty-two cars': a count chip.
On 'two hundred and thirty metres around': an arc measures the lane.

shots.voice: Everyone was told to hold thirty kilometres an hour.
shots.teaches: The rule: a steady 30 km/h.
shots.screen: Close on one side of the ring at a low angle: cars in an even row; a chip 'every driver: 30 km/h' and speed tags on three cars reading 30.
shots.motion: The camera tracks low alongside the cars at their own speed, so they hold still in frame while the ground slides.
shots.transition: The camera rises to the whole ring.
shots.sound: No effect: the bed alone.
shots.check: Tags read 30 km/h (the model's start speed).

frames.note: Closer on one side of the ring: cars in a row, evenly spaced, moving together.
Midway: The camera tracks low alongside the cars at their own speed, so they hold still in frame while the ground slides.
Each car shows the same speed: 30 km/h, and the gaps are equal.

shots.voice: No bottleneck, nothing in the way.
shots.teaches: Nothing in the setup could cause a jam.
shots.screen: The whole ring from low over the infield, turning; chip 'no bottleneck'.
shots.motion: A slow orbit low over the infield while the cars circle evenly.
shots.transition: A soft flash: minutes later.
shots.sound: No effect: the bed alone.
shots.check: The ring is empty but for the cars.

frames.note: Low over the infield: the ring all round, nothing on it but the cars.
Midway: A slow orbit low over the infield while the cars circle evenly.
Chip: no bottleneck. The ring keeps turning.

shots.voice: Within minutes, cars were stopping dead.
shots.teaches: The result: a jam with no cause.
shots.screen: The same ring a few minutes on (chip 'a few minutes later'; 'computer model' tag bottom right): half the ring is packed and red with brake lights, the cars there stopped ('0 km/h').
shots.motion: The camera pushes toward the jam; stopped cars, moving cars.
shots.transition: Rewind to the start, closer.
shots.sound: A low hit on 'stopping dead'.
shots.check: Stopped cars stand still; tag reads 0 km/h.

frames.note: A few minutes on (a chip says so): half the ring is a block of red brake lights.
Midway: The camera pushes toward the jam; stopped cars, moving cars.
Cars at the jam's heart stand still: a 0 km/h tag. Cut: back to the start.

shots.voice: [short pause] Here's why. One driver eases off a little.
shots.teaches: It starts with one small slowdown.
shots.screen: The even ring again, a little closer and set to the left; one car ringed in cyan; its brake lights glow and its tag reads 30 → 25 km/h.
shots.motion: Push toward the marked car; its lights glow for three seconds of model time.
shots.carries: The ring and the marked car.
shots.transition: A glass chart panel opens on the right.
shots.sound: A small click as the lights come on.
shots.check: The others stay calm.

frames.note: Back to the even ring, closer: one car marked in cyan.
Midway: Push toward the marked car; its lights glow for three seconds of model time.
Its brake lights glow; its tag reads 30 then 25 km/h. Everything else is calm.

draw.cut: the chart panel opens on the right

shots.voice: The drivers behind react late and brake harder,
shots.teaches: The slowdown passes back and grows.
shots.screen: Ring left, panel right: 'Lowest speed, driver by driver', one bar per driver as the slowdown reaches them (sim.json 'dips'), each as tall as that driver's lowest speed, 30 km/h full height. The car whose bar is landing glows on the ring.
shots.motion: Model time runs about 1.8 times real time (tagged on screen, worked out so the easing-off lands on 'One' and the stop on 'stops'); bars land one by one in time with the cars.
shots.transition: Continues into the next line, same picture.
shots.sound: Soft ticks for bars, between words.
shots.check: Bar heights are the model's numbers.

frames.note: Ring left, chart right: the first driver's bar stands at 25 km/h.
The brake glow passes back to the next cars; a bar for each driver, as it happens.
Bars start to fall, driver after driver.

shots.voice: so it grows, car after car, until somebody stops.
shots.teaches: The slowdown grows until a car stops.
shots.screen: The bars fall steeply (16, 9, 2, 0 km/h); the last car stops on the ring ('stopped').
shots.motion: The last bar lands at zero; the camera swings to the stopped car.
shots.transition: The panel slides away; the ring fills the frame.
shots.sound: A soft hit on 'stops'.
shots.check: The 19th bar is zero.

frames.note: The bars keep falling, each driver slower than the one ahead.
The bars drop steeply: 16, 9, 2 km/h.
The last bar is zero: a car has stopped (tag on the ring).

draw.cut: the panel slides away; the ring fills the frame

shots.voice: Now watch the jam. The cars go forwards,
shots.teaches: Look at the jam, not the cars: the cars go one way.
shots.screen: The whole ring with its jam; cyan arrows on the moving cars show the way they drive; one car is followed into the back of the jam.
shots.motion: Real model time; the camera tracks the followed car.
shots.transition: The jam gets outlined in red.
shots.sound: No effect: the bed alone.
shots.check: Arrows point the way the cars drive.

frames.note: The whole ring with its jam (red block); arrows on the moving cars point the way they drive.
Midway: Real model time; the camera tracks the followed car.
One car (cyan) is followed as it drives forwards into the back of the jam.

shots.voice: but the jam slides backwards, at about twenty kilometres an hour.
shots.teaches: The jam goes the other way, at about 20 km/h.
shots.screen: A red arc outlines the jam and slides backwards round the ring; a red arrow and chip 'jam: ≈ 20 km/h backwards'.
shots.motion: Real model time (the model's jam moves 18.5 km/h backwards); the arc follows the stopped cars.
shots.transition: The ring flattens into a chart.
shots.sound: A soft whoosh with the backward arrow.
shots.check: Arc and arrow go against the cars.

frames.note: The jam is outlined by a red arc. The cars keep going one way…
…and the red arc slides the other way, round the ring.
Tag on the arc: about 20 km/h, backwards. Cut: the chart.

draw.cut: the ring flattens into a chart

shots.voice: That's a stop-and-go wave. Real highway jams move at that same speed.
shots.teaches: It is a wave, and the same one as on real highways.
shots.screen: A time-and-place chart: every car's trace (time across, place on the ring up), drawn from the model; the flat parts (stopped) line up into a band sloping down; the band is labelled 'stop-and-go wave', a dashed line marks 20 km/h backwards, chip '≈ 20 km/h on real highways too'.
shots.motion: The traces draw left to right as model time runs; the band lights red.
shots.transition: Back to the road, close.
shots.sound: A shimmer as the band lights.
shots.check: The band's slope matches the dashed 20 km/h line closely.

frames.note: A chart of time and place: every car's trace drawn from left to right as time runs.
The jam is where the traces go flat; those flats line up into a band sloping down: backwards.
The slope is labelled: the same ~20 km/h measured on real highways.

shots.voice: [short pause] How do you stop one? Don't tailgate.
shots.teaches: The habit that passes the wave on.
shots.screen: Close, side on, on two cars of the ring: the second right on the first's bumper; when the first brakes the second's lights flare; chip 'tailgating' crossed out.
shots.motion: The camera tracks alongside the pair, side on, as the front car brakes and the second one copies it at once.
shots.transition: The camera drops back.
shots.sound: A small buzz on the cross.
shots.check: Gap reads small.

frames.note: Close on two cars from the side: the second one right on the first one's bumper.
Midway: The camera tracks alongside the pair, side on, as the front car brakes and the second one copies it at once.
The first brakes; the tailgater's brake lights flare instantly. A crossed chip: tailgating.

shots.voice: Leave a big gap, and keep a steady speed.
shots.teaches: The habit that soaks it up: a big gap, a steady speed.
shots.screen: The cyan car ('you', the model's wave-absorbing car) with a long gap bracketed in front; its tag holds a steady speed while the car ahead pulls away.
shots.motion: Camera tracks with the cyan car; the gap bracket stretches as the car ahead accelerates.
shots.transition: Continues: the same car, the gap now shrinking.
shots.sound: No effect: the bed alone.
shots.check: The speed tag holds steady.

frames.note: The cyan car (you) further back, a long gap bracketed in front of it.
Midway: Camera tracks with the cyan car; the gap bracket stretches as the car ahead accelerates.
Its speed tag holds steady while the car ahead speeds up and pulls away.

shots.voice: When the car ahead brakes, don't copy it. Let the gap shrink.
shots.teaches: The gap is the buffer: it shrinks instead of you stopping.
shots.screen: The car ahead stops in the jam (red); the cyan car keeps rolling, lights off, the gap bracket shrinking; the car ahead moves off before the gap is gone.
shots.motion: The camera tracks with the cyan car; the bracket shortens as it rolls up on the stopped car, then the car ahead moves off.
shots.transition: The two speeds become lines on a chart.
shots.sound: No effect between these words.
shots.check: The cyan car never stops.

frames.note: The car ahead hits the jam and stops (red); you roll on slowly, lights off.
The gap shrinks as you roll; you never stop.
The car ahead moves off again just as you arrive. Cut: the two speed lines.

shots.voice: You soak up the wave instead of passing it on.
shots.teaches: Proof in two lines: the wave stops at you.
shots.screen: A chart of speed against time from the model: the car ahead (white) dives to zero and back; you (cyan) run flat; the car behind you (grey) runs flat too.
shots.motion: The three speed lines draw left to right in model time; the white one dives, the cyan and grey stay flat.
shots.transition: The chart fades as the camera rises to the ring.
shots.sound: A soft success chime after 'on'.
shots.check: Lines are the model's speeds.

frames.note: A chart: the car ahead's speed line (white) dives to zero and back; yours (cyan) runs flat.
Midway: The three speed lines draw left to right in model time; the white one dives, the cyan and grey stay flat.
The line of the car behind you is flat too: the wave stops with you.

shots.voice: Later, one car with a computer on the pedals did just that,
shots.teaches: Real evidence: one automated car calmed a whole ring.
shots.screen: The jammed ring; one car ringed in cyan ('one car, speed set by a computer'); source chip 'Stern et al., 2018 · USA'. The ringed car holds its speed and a big gap opens ahead of it.
shots.motion: A slow orbit over the jammed ring in real model time; the ringed car rolls steadily as the gap opens ahead of it.
shots.transition: Model time speeds up on the same picture.
shots.sound: No effect: the bed alone.
shots.check: Chip says the model, not the experiment, is on screen.

frames.note: The ring again, jammed; one car marked as the automated one.
Midway: A slow orbit over the jammed ring in real model time; the ringed car rolls steadily as the gap opens ahead of it.
The marked car holds its speed; a big gap opens in front of it.

shots.voice: and the waves faded.
shots.teaches: The waves die out across the whole ring.
shots.screen: Model time sped up (×8 tag): the red block shrinks and goes; every car rolls at the same speed.
shots.motion: Model time runs eight times faster (tagged), the camera turns slowly; the red lights go out one by one.
shots.transition: The recap cards rise.
shots.sound: A soft rising shimmer as the last lights go out.
shots.check: No brake lights at the end.

frames.note: Time sped up: the red block shrinks lap by lap.
Midway: Model time runs eight times faster (tagged), the camera turns slowly; the red lights go out one by one.
No brake lights left: every car rolling at the same speed.

shots.voice: [warmly] So a jam out of nowhere starts with one tap on the brakes.
shots.teaches: The answer in three pictures.
shots.screen: Three glass cards over the dimmed ring: 'one tap grows' (falling bars, the model's), 'the jam goes backwards' (a ring with a red backward arrow), 'a gap soaks it up' (the cyan car and its gap).
shots.motion: Cards rise in turn; their small pictures draw.
shots.transition: The cards fall away.
shots.sound: A card sound each.
shots.check: The small bars are the same numbers as s12.

frames.note: The recap: three glass cards rise in a row over the calm ring.
Midway: Cards rise in turn; their small pictures draw.
Each card holds its small picture: falling bars; a red arc with a backward arrow; the cyan car with its gap.

shots.voice: And it can end with you.
shots.teaches: The payoff: the viewer can stop it.
shots.screen: The calm ring, the cyan car leading a smooth line; the line to remember lands: 'Leave a gap. Soak up the wave.'
shots.motion: A slow pull back over the calm ring; the title types in by character and a sheen crosses its accent.
shots.transition: Holds into the poster.
shots.sound: THE PAYOFF: a warm hit as the title lands.
shots.check: Title contrast.

frames.note: The calm ring, every car moving, the cyan one leading a smooth line.
Midway: A slow pull back over the calm ring; the title types in by character and a sheen crosses its accent.
